title: Locale registry
description: The languages the experience can be read in, their authoring budgets, and the locale profile: what each language IS, declared once, so that build, CSS and runtime read these facts and never infer them from a language name. See docs/text-experience-binding.md, Language differences.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint; not part of the data.

sourceLocale.description: The language of the original public-domain text in text/raw/.

baseLocale.description: The retelling every translation works from.

maxChars.description: Authoring budget per segment. A limit on how long a sentence may be written, not a promise that it fits one rendered line.

dir.description: Base writing direction for this language's text.

lineBreak.description: CSS line-break keyword a scene should apply to this language's text.

significantSpaces.description: True when spaces inside a segment are authored content, as in the Japanese phrase spacing. Such text must never be trimmed, collapsed, or re-wrapped by a template or a minifier.

setApart.description: How this language marks a word that is on display (written on a thing, named as a word), in order of preference: 'quotes' is any paired quotation marks, corner brackets included; 'capitals' is an all-capitals run of two or more letters, a capitalised word of five or more letters, or a capital standing alone as a letter. scripts/check-experience.py verifies a demo's declared reads against exactly these methods.

wordUnit.description: How a line is split into the units a stage lights or lays out one at a time (sung words, the tail's chunks, a label's two lines): 'spaces' when the language writes its units with spaces between them (phrase spaces count), 'segmenter' when it does not, so Intl.Segmenter finds the words. One helper implements both: units() in src/demos/shell/words.ts.

emphasis.description: How speech and thought are set apart from narration: 'italic' where the script has an italic, 'slip' (a warmer slip, never a synthesised slant) where it does not. Written to the page as data-emphasis.

glyphWidth.description: Whether the script's glyphs fill the em box ('full': CJK, kana, Hangul) or not ('half'). Drives the smaller caption size and the looser leading; written to the page as data-glyph-width. For a mixed run, isWide() in words.ts remains the per-character truth.

numbers.description: The Intl locale tag numbers (and words, for the segmenter) are formatted with, e.g. 'en-GB', 'ja-JP'. A demo never passes the page's lang to Intl itself; it asks shell.locale.
